title.t: A lead's score lands exactly on a tier line

when.t: A lead's score equals a tier threshold.

steps.t: Agent 02 gives the lead the lower tier.
It tells the authorized user the score sat on a tier line and the lower tier was given.
steps.src: dispatcher/listing_spokes_02.py::if any("sits exactly on a tier boundary" in n for n in notes):; check:02-01:envelope.persisted:clarification.request

never.t: Assign the higher tier on a boundary.

you_see.t: A question naming the score and the tier given.

test.t: The signed rubric: a budget of 400,000 or more scores 40, a timeline of 30 days or less scores 40, a pre-approval scores 20; a score above 40 is warm and above 70 is hot (a score exactly on 40 or 70 gets the lower tier and a question). A lead with a 450,000 budget, a 90-day timeline and no financing scores exactly 40 and is recorded cold.

title.t: There is no signed scoring rubric

when.t: A lead arrives to be scored and no signed rubric is in force.

steps.t: Agent 02 does not score the lead; its tier is unknown.
It tells the authorized user scoring is halted because no rubric is active. No hot-lead alert is raised.

never.t: Score from memory of a rubric.

you_see.t: A question saying no rubric is active.

test.t: The system starts without a signed rubric; a lead with a 500,000 budget and a 10-day timeline comes in.

steps.t: The rule: hot, whatever the score.
Agent 01 passes the demand on with the captured lead (owner decision of 2026-10-28), so the lead goes to the hot-lead queue whatever its score, with the call clock.

never.t: Let a score decide for a lead who demanded a person.

you_see.t: A hot-lead alert quoting the request for a person, with the call clock, for a lead whose budget and timeline alone score cold; the tier record says hot because of the demand.

test.t: A call says "Can I please speak to a person?", with a 150,000 budget and a 200-day timeline (cold on the rubric).

title.t: A lead says it is urgent but shows no financing

when.t: A lead states high urgency and no financing progress.

steps.t: Agent 02 scores financing and timeline as given; stated urgency adds nothing.
It writes the conflict into the tier record.

never.t: Raise a score for stated urgency.

you_see.t: The conflict in the lead's tier record.

test.t: A lead with "high" urgency, no financing, a 450,000 budget and a 60-day timeline (its score of 40 is also on the warm line, so it is recorded cold and the authorized user is asked).

when.t: A lead's tier returns to a value it just left (for example hot, cold, hot).

steps.t: Agent 02 scores each inquiry as it comes.
On the swing back it asks the authorized user to review, with the tier history.

never.t: Keep re-tiering a swinging lead without telling anyone.

why.t: The tuple's words: oscillation is a signal, not noise.

you_see.t: A question saying the tier swung a third time, with the history.

test.t: Three inquiries on one client score hot, cold, then hot. The third also raises a hot-lead alert.

title.t: A signed rubric tries to change a fixed rule

when.t: A signed rubric contains settings beyond the seven thresholds and weights.

steps.t: Agent 02 reads only the seven scoring settings; the extra ones are never read.
It tells the authorized user which settings it ignored.

never.t: Let a rubric override a fixed rule, or drop the conflict silently.

why.t: The tuple's words: a surfaced conflict is a finding; a silent pick is drift.

you_see.t: A question naming the ignored settings.

test.t: A signed rubric "t-extra" with the usual weights plus "demands_human_weight": 0.

title.t: A lead's pre-approval letter has expired

when.t: A lead's pre-approval letter is marked expired.

steps.t: Agent 02 gives no financing points, even if the lead also says they are pre-approved.
The note "pre-approval letter expired" goes in the tier record.

never.t: Count an expired letter as financing.

you_see.t: The expired-letter note with the score.

test.t: A lead with a 500,000 budget, a 20-day timeline and an expired letter scores 80: budget and timeline only.

title.t: The lead is an agent shopping for a client

when.t: An inquiry is marked as an agent shopping for a client.

steps.t: Agent 02 does not score it.
It asks the authorized user how to engage; no hot-lead alert is raised.

never.t: Score another agent as a consumer lead.

you_see.t: A question saying this is an agent-to-agent inquiry.

test.t: An agent-shopping inquiry with a 700,000 budget, 10 days and pre-approval (hot if scored).

when.t: A rubric change arrives without a valid signature.

steps.t: The dispatcher refuses it as an integrity violation and notifies the authorized user; Agent 02 never receives it.
Scoring continues on the last signed rubric.

you_see.t: An integrity alert; scores keep the signed rubric's version.

test.t: An unsigned rubric with a budget threshold of 100 arrives. A lead with a 300,000 budget and a 90-day timeline then scores cold on the signed rubric "synth-v1".

title.t: A lead's stated budget differs from the pre-approval amount

when.t: A stated budget differs from the amount on the pre-approval document.

steps.t: Agent 02 scores on the document's amount.
The conflict goes in the tier record word for word.

never.t: Score on the stated budget when the document differs.

test.t: A lead says 600,000; the pre-approval is for 350,000. The score is 60 and the lead goes to follow-up as warm.

title.t: A re-score arrives while a hot alert is open

when.t: A re-score request arrives for a lead whose hot alert has not been closed.
when.src: dispatcher/listing_spokes_02.py::if env.intent == "lead.rescored" and ctx in self.open_escalations:

steps.t: Agent 02 does not re-score; it holds the request and asks the authorized user.
steps.src: dispatcher/listing_spokes_02.py::if env.intent == "lead.rescored" and ctx in self.open_escalations:; check:02-11:envelope.persisted:clarification.request

never.t: Re-tier a lead during an open hot alert.

why.t: The tuple's words: the authorized user's read outranks the rubric during an open alert.

you_see.t: A question saying a re-score arrived during an open alert.

test.t: A hot lead raises an alert; a re-score with lower numbers then arrives. Stand-in: Agent 03 re-scores only warm leads, so the test sends it as Agent 03.

title.t: Nothing is known about a lead's budget, timeline or financing

when.t: A lead gives none of the facts the rubric uses.

steps.t: Agent 02 records the tier as unknown, not cold.
It asks the authorized user.

never.t: Treat missing facts as a low score.

why.t: The tuple's words: unknown is absent data, not a low score.

you_see.t: A question saying all scoring inputs are unknown.

test.t: A web form with only a name and an email.

title.t: The scoring engine is below the confidence floor

when.t: The engine's confidence is below the floor: 0.45 unless the authorized user signs another (decision_engine confidence_floor).

steps.t: Agent 02 holds the lead and asks the authorized user to continue or cancel.
Continue: the lead is scored with the signed rubric and acted on. Cancel: archived, nothing sent.

never.t: Act on a tier under the floor.

you_see.t: A held lead asking continue or cancel.

test.t: The authorized user signs a floor of 0.9; the local engine reports 0.85. The authorized user continues: the signed rubric scores it hot and a hot-lead alert follows.

title.t: Lead data would go to the outside scoring service

when.t: The outside decision engine could score a lead.

steps.t: Lead data goes out only when a service key is installed and the authorized user has signed that it may.
Otherwise nothing is sent and the local engine scores.

never.t: Send lead data because a key is installed.

you_see.t: The score; the record shows the local engine made it.

test.t: The authorized user signs "allow external" with no key installed. A lead comes in: nothing goes out and the local engine scores it.

title.t: The scoring engine returns a tier nobody knows

when.t: The engine returns a tier Agent 02 does not recognize.

steps.t: Agent 02 treats it as below the floor and holds the lead for the authorized user (as in 02-13).
steps.src: dispatcher/listing_spokes_02.py::tier = "HELD_FOR_CALIBRATION"   # an engine answer this agent cannot act on holds

steps.t: No way in yet: this needs a live engine; the test runner has no key.

you_see.t: A held lead asking continue or cancel.

title.t: A warm lead goes to follow-up with its scoring facts

steps.t: Agent 02 sends the lead to Agent 03 with its scoring facts.
steps.src: dispatcher/listing_spokes_02.py::inputs = {k: payload[k] for k in RESCORE_INPUT_KEYS if k in payload}; check:02-16:envelope.persisted:lead.nurture

steps.t: Agent 03 uses them for its weekly re-score.
steps.src: dispatcher/listing_spokes_03.py::def rescore_cadence(self, ctx: str, today: str):

never.t: Pass a warm lead on without its scoring facts.

you_see.t: Nothing extra; the lead starts its follow-up.

test.t: A lead with a 500,000 budget, a 60-day timeline and pre-approval scores warm.
